7.3.8.3.5 Building ISD Names 
ISDLINK supports names configured using either single- or multiple-byte character sets. The 
rules are slightly different for each type of character set. 
• Single-Byte Character Set 
When a data item is to be exchanged with an ISDLINK remote, the data item 
identification or an ISD optional name must be built from the SCADA hierarchy of 
Substation, Device Type, Device, and either Analog, Count, or Point IDs. Each ID must be 
separated from the next one by a blank, a dollar sign, or an underscore. The dollar sign 
and underscore characters can be used only if neither of the IDs already has these 
characters. ISDLINK looks first for blank, then dollar, then underscore; blank must not be 
used for the data item identification (use only in the ISD optional name). 
Maximum ID lengths are: 
– SUBSTN = 8 
– DEVTYP = 6 
– DEVICE = 14 
– POINT, ANALOG, COUNT = 4 
The SCADA IDs: 
– Cannot have embedded blanks 
– Can contain any printable ASCII character (except the one used as a separator) 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 436 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
Examples of valid and invalid ISD names: 
LAKEVIEW$PLC$LV1_CONTROLER$SPFB Valid as data item iden tification and as optional 
name. 
LAKEVIEW_PLC_LV1_CONTROLER_SPFB Invalid: Un derscore cannot be used as separator 
because one of the IDs already contains this 
character. 
LAKEVIEW PLC000 LV1_CONTROLER SPFB Valid as ISD optional na me but invalid as data item 
identification. 
• Multiple-Byte Character Set 
When a data item is to be exchanged with an ISDLINK remote using a multi-byte 
character set, an ISD optional name must be used. It is built from the SCADA hierarchy 
of Substation, Device Type, Device, and either Analog, Count, or Point IDs. Each ID must 
be separated from the next one by a blank. 
Maximum ID lengths depend on how many bytes are needed to represent a single 
character. The maximum number of bytes (not characters) allowed is: 
– SUBSTN = 8 
– DEVTYP = 6 
– DEVICE = 14 
– POINT, ANALOG, COUNT = 4 
The SCADA IDs cannot have embedded blanks. 
You must define an environment variable to enable multi-byte character support at run 
time. For more information, refer to the e-terracomm Software Installation and 
Maintenance Guide. 
Note: Currently, only the Korean character set is supported. 
7.3.8.3.6 Building HABCLINK Names 
The name provided to HABCLINK must be in the form “field,compositekey” (excluding the 
quotes, but including the comma) in which: 
• field is the e-terrahabitat field_record name. For example: 
– OPEN_LN2: A True/False bit on the LN2 record 
– PEAKTIME_UNIT: An R*4 field on the LN2 record 
– TOPDELAY: A global item 
You can use the full complement of HABConnect specifications, as defined in the 
HABConnect User’s Guide (“Specifying an e-terrahabitat Link – Specifying the Topic”). For 
example: 
– I$BS_ND>KV_BS: An R*4 field on the BS record pointed to by the ND record 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 437 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• compositekey is the e-terrahabitat composite key. Except for ranges and subscripts, you 
can use the full complement of HABConnect specifications, as defined in the 
HABConnect User’s Guide (“Specifying an e-terrahabitat Link – Specifying the Item”). For 
example: 
– TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.DOUGLAS.10.T538 
For OPEN_LN2 in the NETMOM database: ID_DECK.ID_CO.ID_DV.ID_ST.ID_ND.ID_LN2 
– TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.LAKEVIEW.38 
For I$BS_ND>KV_BS: DECK in the NETMOM database: 
ID_DECK.ID_CO.ID_DV.ID_ST.ID_ND 
Range specifications that are undetected during validation cause a run-time error. 
Subscripts provoke a warning during validation; they are discouraged because 
subscripts can change very easily in the target e-terrahabitat database. HABCLINK and 
HABConnect Sampler do not know the difference, and they fetch or deposit the wrong 
data without objection. 
Some complete names are: 
• OPEN_LN2,TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.DOUGLAS.10.T538 
• I$BS_ND>KV_BS,TOPOLOGY.NEPOOL.EAST.LAKEVIEW.38

ISDLINK differentiates them by the network type (see the display Data Items 
Permissions/Network Type). 
• Size: Must be filled for non-SCADA data items. This is the size of the largest message 
that can be received or transmitted. 
– For Information Message (INFOMSG): The size of the data item must be the size of 
the buffer to send plus 14 bytes for the ICCP Block 4 header, since this is the amount 
of space allocated by OAGSERVE, not the size of the data part of the message. 
– The size of an Account Request (ACTREQ) data item must be 30. 
– The size of a Control Message (CTRLMSG) data item must be 20.

(T*4) and the value transferred between HABConnect Sampler and HABCLINK should be

ELCOLINK ELCOLINK allows the definition of  special data items called “ELCOM_PARTNER1”, 
“ELCOM_PARTNER2”, ..., “ELCOM_PARTNERn”. One for each remote partner that must be

each remote partner. They have value ON for communication UP and value OFF for 
communication DOWN with each remote partner. 
Other Link 
Applications 
Not used. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 441 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• Source remote: Specify the remote source of the data item. 
• ICCP scope: The ICCP protocol allows data items to be created with either “VMD scope” 
or “Domain scope”. 
When a data item is created with “VMD scope”, only one MMS named variable is created 
for that data item, regardless of the number of remotes with access. Unauthorized 
requests for that data item are not refused until ICCPLINK processes the request. 
When a data item is created with “Domain scope”, the number of MMS named variables 
created for that data item is equal to the number of remotes with access to that data 
item. Unauthorized requests for that data item are refused immediately by MMS. 
A general rule to apply is to set a data item’s scope to “VMD scope” if more than one 
remote has Read access to it, and set the scope to “Domain scope” if only one remote 
has Read access to it. However, all data items can be configured with VMD scope, the 
only access control being through appropriate setting of the Read permission. 
• Data conversion: You can specify a CommDataConversion record that should be used 
for data item–specific conversion (see section 7.3.6 Data Semantics Conversion). 
7.3.8.5 Control Devices 
CommControlDevice records are used to model supervisory controls associated with 
CommDataItems. 
• Name: Enter the identifier of the device. For ICCP, this is an MMS identifier; therefore, it 
must begin with a letter and contain the characters [a...z], [A...Z], [0...9], $, and _ 
(underscore) only. It must not duplicate data item identification or the ICCP optional 
name. If the device is Select Before Operate (SBO), the name length must not exceed 
24 characters because ICCPLINK has to build a name such as “<ICCP device 
name>_success” (concatenation of up to 8 characters). For a Direct Operate (DO) device, 
the maximum length is 32 characters. If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK, 
and no ICCPLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field 
can be left blank. 
• ICCP scope: The ICCP protocol allows devices to be created with either “VMD scope” or 
“Domain scope”. 
– VMD scope: only one MMS named variable is created for that device, regardless of 
the number of remotes with access. Unauthorized requests for that device are not 
refused until ICCPLINK processes the request. 
– Domain scope: the number of MMS named variables created for that device is equal 
to the number of remotes with access to that device. Unauthorized requests for that 
device are refused immediately by MMS. 
A general rule to apply is to set a device’s scope to “VMD scope” if more than one 
remote has Execute permission to it, and set the scope to “Domain scope” if only one 
remote has Execute permission to it. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 442 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
A device and the data item with which it is associated can have different scopes. It 
makes sense, for example, that all remotes can read the data item value (data item in 
VMD scope), but only one can control the associated device (device in Domain scope). 
• ISD site name: This is the site originating command/setpoint on the device. If the control 
is not passing through ISDLINK, and no ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to 
the parent data item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through 
ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent 
data item, this field must be filled with any two characters. For more information, see 
section 7.8 InterSite Control 1.0. 
• Class: Specify whether the device is a Select Before Operate (SBO) or Direct Operate (DO) 
device. For more information, see section 7.8 InterSite Control 1.0. 
• Timeout: Time, in seconds, that an SBO device stays in the armed state after a 
successful Select operation. This field is relevant for SBO devices only. If an Operate 
operation on the device is not received within this time, the device is de-selected and 
returns to the idle state. If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK, and no ICCPLINK 
remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field can be left blank. 
If the control is not passing through ICCPLINK, but one of the ICCPLINK remotes has 
Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field must be filled with a valid 
value (> 0). 
• Check back name: This is an arbitrary number, agreed upon by the ICCP partners, that 
the ICCP server returns to the client as a result of a Select operation. The client can then 
check that the returned value is the expected one; whether to make this check is a client 
issue. If ICCPLINK is acting as a client, it always checks the returned value. If the value 
does not match the expected one, ICCPLINK logs an error and does not send the 
Operate request. This field is relevant for SBO devices only. Leave it blank if the control is 
not passing through ICCPLINK. 
• Intersite control 0/1 name: For digital status, these are the names of the commands 
sent to a remote site that represent a 0 (ICCP_OPEN) and a 1 (ICCP_CLOSE), respectively. 
They must match the names configured in the SCADA Command record because 
matching a command between SCADA and ISDLINK is done by name. If the control is 
not passing through ISDLINK, and no ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to 
the parent data item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through 
ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent 
data item, this field must be filled (any string). 
• Intersite setpoint name: This is the name of a setpoint. It must match the name 
configured in the SCADA Setpoint record because matching a setpoint between SCADA 
and ISDLINK is done by name. If the control is not passing through ISDLINK, and no 
ISDLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field can be 
left blank. If the control is not passing through ISDLINK, but one of the ISDLINK remotes 
has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field must be filled (any 
string). 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 443 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• ELCOM group/point: ELCOM group and point ID for the control. It is a numeric value 
between 1 (for group) or 0 (for point) and 255. If the control is not passing through 
ELCOLINK, and no ELCOLINK remote has Read or Write permission to the parent data 
item, this field can be left blank. If the control is not passing through ELCOLINK, but one 
of the ELCOLINK remotes has Read or Write permission to the parent data item, this field 
must be filled with a valid value. 
Note: There is nothing to configure for support of ICCP Conformance Block 7 (Events). 
ICCPLINK automatically enrolls in the four pre-defined event conditions for SBO devices 
(Timeout, Local Reset, Success, and Failure) if the remote site owning the SBO device also 
supports ICCP Conformance Block 7 (the phrase “owning the device” means that the 
remote has Write permission to the data item the device is child of). 
As a server, ICCPLINK supports the three ICCP defined operations: Create Event Enrollment, 
Delete Event Enrollment, and Get Event Enrollment Attributes. ICCPLINK supports the Event 
Notification action. All pre-defined event conditions are supported (Access Violation, Data 
Failure, and the four SBO devices’ related event conditions). ICCPLINK triggers the Success 
and Failure events only when ISDLINK is using InterSite Controls 1.0. 
As a client, ICCPLINK only supports the Create Event Enrollment operation for the four 
pre-defined event conditions for SBO devices. It never enrolls in Access Violation or Data 
Failure event conditions. Success and Failure events received from the server are passed to 
ISDLINK but reach the EMS only if InterSite Controls 1.0 is used. 
Note: Support for ICCP Conformance Block 7 can be disabled (see the “ICCPLINK Options” 
section of the e-terracomm Software Installation and Maintenance Guide). 
7.3.8.6 Optional Name 
The CommDataItemName record is used to model additional or optional names for data 
items. 
• Name: Enter the optional name. This character string has a maximum length of 60 
characters. The actual maximum depends on the protocol (see section 7.3.8.3.7 Data 
Item Identification or Optional Names Restrictions Based on Protocol). For 
CommDataItemName records associated with ISDLINK, enter the association to the 
measurement instead. 
• Name for: Use the picklist to choose the protocol that the optional name is for. 
• Measurement: For names associated with ISDLINK, the CommDataItemName record 
should point to the associated SCADA measurement in e-terrasource. During export, the 
ISD name of the measurement is automatically computed and filled in the e-terracomm 
model instead of the Name field. During import, the linkage between 
CommDataitemName records and SCADA measurements is automatically performed 
when SCADAMOM and OAGMOM are imported together. Otherwise, a sample script 
(Link_CommDataItemName_Measurement.sql) is provided to assist in linking 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 444 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
CommDataItemName records to the correct SCADA Analog, Discrete, and Accumulator 
records. Refer to the e-terrasource Software Installation and Maintenance Guide for 
more information on this script. 
7.3.8.7 Limit Sets 
The CommLimitSet record is used to model the limit sets associated with a given data item. 
Only data items with a base type of REAL32 can have limit sets. Any number of limit sets 
can be associated with a data item. The actual number depends on the number of limits 
modeled in SCADA and whether some limits are relevant for remote sites. 
• Name: Name of the limit set for ICCP exchange. It must follow the same ICCP naming 
rules as for data items, and it must not exceed 28 characters because “_L” or “_H” is 
added to create two REAL32 named variables, one for the low and one for the high limit 
values (the size limit is set to 28 for possible future expansion to more than two values 
for a limit set). 
• ISD name: ISD name of the limit, which must match the name modeled in SCADA 
(Substation, Device Type, Device, Analog, Limit). Naming follows the ISD naming rules. 
• Disable high limit check: If Yes, the high limit is not checked. 
• Disable low limit check: If Yes, the low limit is not checked. 
Note: The number of limits modeled for a given data item is what you make available for 
ICCP remotes or what you want to receive from ICCP remotes. It does not mean that 
remotes request all the limits you have made available, or that you can receive all the 
limits you have modeled. Only the high or low limit may be available from a remote, or you 
may decide to make available only the low or high limit of a limit set. Partial ICCP data 
sets are created when not all requested limits are available, as for non-limit data items. 
Limit sets’ Read/Write permissions are inherited from the parent data item.

7.3.9 Data Sets 
7.3.9.1 Definition 
The purpose of CommDataSets is to group data items according to the reporting 
preferences of the parent remote. For uniformity of modeling, e-terracomm uses the data 
set record to hold trigger, reporting style, and timing information even for non-SCADA data 
items. The data set structure does not prevent ICCP sites from reading and writing 
individual data items — indeed, for Block 8 and Block 4, data sets are invisible to the remote 
ICCP sites. 
The data sets themselves are modeled using the CommDataSet record, whereas the data 
items within the data sets are referenced with CommDataSetDataItem records. 
Not all data sets need to be modeled. It depends on which protocol the data sets are for. 
7.3.9.1.1 Protocol-Specific Modeling 
ICCPLINK Output data sets do not need to be crea ted at modeling time. It is the ICCP client’s 
responsibility to check that data sets exist on the server (output data sets) and, if not, 
create them. Note that, if output data sets are modeled, the attributes (Trigger, Style, etc.) 
are overwritten by the remote site when it enables the data set. 
Data sets can reference both data items and limit sets. 
ISDLINK Only one output data set per remote is  allowed. Output data set parameters must be 
modeled, but the content of the output data set does not need to be modeled. It is the 
client’s (the EMS host) responsibility to tell ISDLINK which data items it wants to receive. 
Input data sets must be fully modeled, including transmission parameters and contents. 
Data sets can reference both data items and limit sets. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 448 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
HABCLINK Input and output data sets must be fully modeled, transmission parameters and 
contents. 
Limit sets are not allowed. 
FILELINK Only one input or one ou tput data set per link per remote is allowed. This data set must 
be PERIODIC with a reporting style of ALL. FILELINK data sets can contain only REAL, 
INTEGER, and STATUS type data items. 
Limit sets are not allowed. 
ELCOLINK Input data sets must be modeled while output data sets can be modeled, or the creation 
and deletion can be done by the remote site at run time. Both modeled and dynamically 
created data sets are supported and can coexist for a given remote. If Group 
Management functions are not supported, the output data sets must be modeled. 
Limit sets are not allowed. 
The CommDataSet properties are detailed below. 
• Name: The identifier of the data set. This is a string of 32 characters or fewer with no 
embedded blanks. It must be unique within the remote. See below for protocol-specific 
restrictions. 
ICCPLINK Must begin with a letter. Only  alphanumeric characters (0–9, a–z, 
A–Z) and $ and _ (underscore) characters are allowed. 
ISDLINK No specific restrictions. 
HABCLINK No specific restrictions. 
FILELINK No specific restrictions. 
ELCOLINK Must be a number between 1 and 32767. This is the ELCOM-90 group number. 
• In service: In/out of service default setting. 
• Data set type: Picklist to select Input or Output. An input data set contains incoming 
data (from a remote to e-terracomm). An output data set contains outgoing data (from 
e-terracomm to a remote). 
• Trigger: Picklist to select when the data set is sent (Output) or when it is supposed to be 
received (Input). e-terracomm supports the triggers listed below, but not all protocols 
support all triggers (see protocol-specific information after the description of the 
Transmission Style field below). 
– Periodic: Data set is input/output on a periodic basis. 
– Exception: Data set is input/output when an exception occurs (data value and/or 
attribute of a data item in the data set has changed). 
– On request: Data set is input/output upon request. 
– On receipt: For output data sets only. The data set is output upon receipt of its twin 
data set. 
– Periodic data transfer (ELCOM only): The periodicity is given by the priority class 
(see the Serial Number/Priority Class fields). 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 449 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
– Periodically requested data transfer (ELCOM only): ELCOLINK polls the remote for 
these data sets at the modeled periodic rate, which is given by the priority class (see 
the Serial Number/Priority Class fields). 
– Unsolicited data transfer: ELCOLINK unsolicited or unsolicited mixed data transfer. 
For ISDLINK and ICCPLINK, this is the same as trigger by exception, except that all 
changes occurring during the buffering time are reported (for details, see section 
7.9.2 New Way of Reporting Data Changes). The transmission style must be Report 
by Exception. 
• Transmission style: Picklist to select All (all data items in the data set are transmitted), 
or Report by Exception (RBE, only data items that have their value or attributes change 
are transmitted). 
The Exception trigger and the Report by Exception transmission style govern different 
characteristics of the data set. It is entirely reasonable to define a data set that is 
triggered upon change of value, but reports all its data items, even the unchanged ones. 
Trigger and transmission style restrictions apply, depending on data types and protocol. 
A data set carrying SCADA data is called a “SCADA data set”; a data set carrying 
non-SCADA data is called a “non-SCADA data set”. A given data set cannot carry both 
SCADA and non-SCADA data. 
Non-SCADA data sets (Account Objects, Info Message, and Control messages) must be 
configured as follows: 
– Input data sets must have Trigger set to On Request and Transmission Style set to 
All. 
– Output data sets must have Trigger set to On Receipt and Transmission Style set to 
All. 
7.3.9.1.2 Protocol-Specific Modeling 
ICCPLINK SCADA data sets: 
Input: Trigger = Periodic, On Request, Exception, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = All or 
RBE. 
Output: Trigger = Periodic, Exception, On Receipt, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = All or 
RBE. 
Non-SCADA data sets: see the section above. 
ISDLINK SCADA data sets have restricted triggers and transmission styles: 
Input: Trigger = Periodic; Style = RBE. The periodicity is the polling rate. 
Output: Trigger = Exception, Unsolicited Data Transfer; Style = RBE. 
Non-SCADA data sets: see the section above. 
HABCLINK Data sets have re stricted trigger settings: 
Input: Trigger = Periodic or On Request. 
Output: Trigger = Periodic, Exception, On Receipt. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 450 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
FILELINK FILELINK data sets have restricted trigger and transmission style settings: 
Input: Trigger = Periodic and Style = All. 
Output: Trigger = Periodic and Style = All. 
ELCOLINK Trigger: Periodic and Exception are invalid. On Request, Periodically Requested Data 
Transfer, and Periodic Data Transfer must have Style = All. Unsolicited Data Transfer must 
have Style = RBE. 
• Data item count: This is a non-enterable (calculated) field that displays the number of 
CommDataSetDataItem children in the data set. 
• Exception buffering time: This is the exception buffering time in seconds. The exception 
buffering time applies only to output data sets that are triggered by Exception (or 
Unsolicited Data Transfer for ICCPLINK). This field designates the amount of time 
OAGSERVE waits (in case other changed values arrive) before shipping out the data set. 
Its purpose is to avoid triggering the same data set multiple times within a short period. 
For Unsolicited Data Transfer data sets, the buffering time is not monitored by 
OAGSERVE. Instead: 
– For ICCP, ICCPLINK does the monitoring. 
– For ISD, the buffering time is actually the EMS polling interval (i.e., value changes are 
buffered between consecutive polls). 
By default, the exception buffering time is set equal to the global default buffering time 
(see section 7.3.2 e-terracomm Configuration Parameters). To specify a different value, 
set the Override global exception buffering time field to Yes, then enter the desired time 
in the Exception buffering time field. 
• Periodic timer: For output data sets, this property specifies how often the data set is 
shipped out. If the data set’s style is RBE and no data item values/attributes have 
changed, a transmit message (with a zero data item count) is nonetheless sent to the 
link application. Depending upon the protocol, the link application may or may not ship 
a report to the remote. For input data sets, this property specifies how often the data set 
is expected. The timer is synchronized to the receipt of the first report. The period is 
specified in seconds. 
• Grace percentage: For input data sets, the grace percentage is used to calculate how 
long OAGSERVE should wait after the periodic timer or the integrity timer expires, before 
deciding that the report is late. When a report is late, all of its data items are marked 
invalid (“No current reading available”). By default, the grace percentage is set equal to 
the global grace period for reception value (see section 7.3.2 e-terracomm 
Configuration Parameters). To specify a different percentage, set the Override global 
grace percentage flag to Yes, and enter a value for the grace percentage. There is a 
minimum value of 1% for the grace percentage. The grace percentage is not used by 
output data sets. 
• Integrity timer: Used by data sets that are triggered by exception, and by periodic data 
sets whose transmission style is Report by Exception. When the integrity timer expires, 
OAGSERVE transmits the output data set or expects the input data set. The grace 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 451 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
percentage is also used by OAGSERVE in the same manner for the integrity period as for 
the Period. The integrity timer is specified in seconds. 
7.3.9.1.3 Protocol-Specific Modeling 
ISDLINK The integrity timer must be 0 for input data sets (due to the way EMS sends integrity 
scans — separate for status, analogs, an d counts, a few points at a time). 
Output data sets must have a non-zero integrity period to make sure that ISDLINK sends 
all current values as soon as a connection is established. 
ICCPLINK 
HABCLINK 
FILELINK 
For output exception data sets (trigger is Exception or Unsolicited Data Transfer, or 
trigger is Periodic and transmission style is Report By Exception), the value should be > 0; 
otherwise, data is sent only when changes are detected. This can take a long time and, 
after a connection with the remote is established, data remains invalid until a change is 
detected. When the integrity period is not 0, all data is sent as soon as a connection with 
the remote is established. 
ELCOLINK ELCOM-90 does not ha ve integrity scans defined. 
• Twin data set: Identity of the twin data set. Each pair of twin data sets must contain one 
input and one output. They must name each other as their twin. The lists of their 
contents (CommDataSetDataItem records) must match exactly. The input twin can have 
any trigger, and the output twin must be triggered on receipt. The twin of a critical 
(end-to-end acknowledgment requested) data set must also be defined as critical. Each 
critical or non-SCADA data set must have a twin. 
• Legal application: For HABCLINK data sets only. This specifies the identity of a 
CommLegalApplication record associated with the data set. 
• Data item holding data set state: For input data sets, you can specify the identifier of 
the data item used to hold the state of the data set (Not Active, Active, Late). Modeling of 
the data item is detailed in section 7.10.3.2 Data Set Component Data Items. 
• Control timeout: For ICCPLINK and ISDLINK control message data sets, this is the device 
timeout. A Select Before Operate (SBO) device returns to the idle state if no response to a 
Select or Operate request is received within the specified time. This timeout is for 
messages exchanged internally between link applications (e.g., ICCPLINK forwarding an 
Operate request received from a remote site to ISDLINK to be passed to EMS). 
Note: When defining ICCPLINK control data sets, make sure that the device timeout at 
the remote site (if e-terracomm is used) is shorter than the end-to-end flow control 
timer T2 (if flow control is enabled); otherwise, failure to receive a response for a device 
can trigger the abort of the association. 
• Periodic offset: For ELCOM input data sets with trigger Periodic Data Transfer or 
Periodically Requested Data Transfer, or output data sets with trigger Periodic and 
FILELINK input data sets, it is possible to specify a relative time offset. 
Data sets with periods of an integer number of days can be scheduled to be shipped at 
a given hour:minute:second within the first day (the “first” day is the one in which the 
offset occurs following the startup of the data set). 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 452 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
Data sets with periods of an integer number of minutes can be scheduled to be shipped 
at a given second within the first minute (the “first” minute is the one in which the offset 
occurs following the startup of the data set). 
Data sets with periods of an integer number of hours can be scheduled to be shipped at 
a given minute:second offset within the first hour (the “first” hour is the one in which the 
offset occurs following the startup of the data set). 
The offset is specified as a date where the month, day, and year are ignored. 
• Periodic offset type: This is a picklist that allows you to specify whether the periodic 
offset is relative to the time the link application started, or is synchronized to the wall 
clock. 
• Partial data set allowed: When used for ICCPLINK, it applies to input ICCPLINK data sets 
only: 
– If Yes, the corresponding output data set is created at the remote site even when 
some of its data items are not available. 
– If No, the corresponding output data set is not created at the remote site when some 
of its data items are not available. 
When used for FILELINK, it applies to input FILELINK data sets only. 
– If Yes, the dataset is read from the file even if data items are missing. 
– If No, the data items are not loaded unless all of the data items are present in the file 
for the data set. 
The steps to create partial data sets are detailed in the e-terracomm User’s Guide – 
Real-Time Operation. Note that the flag is only relevant for SCADA data sets. 
• Ack: Set to Yes if local acknowledgement is requested. 
• Critical: Set to Yes if end-to-end acknowledgement is requested. 
Local and end-to-end acknowledgment cannot both be requested. Non-SCADA data 
sets do not support any kind of acknowledgment. 
7.3.9.1.4 Protocol-Specific Modeling 
ICCPLINK Supports both local and end-to -end acknowledgment for SCADA data sets. 
ISDLINK Does not support an y kind of acknowledgment. 
HABCLINK Does not support  local acknowledgment. 
FILELINK Does not support an y kind of acknowledgment. 
ELCOLINK Does not support an y kind of acknowledgment. 
• ELCOM priority class: For ELCOLINK, the priority class is a number between 0 and 15. 
The number is used as an index in a table that contains, for each index, the period (in 
seconds) to be used for the data set. Default values are hard-coded. They can be 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 453 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
overridden by the values found in a configuration file (for details about the configuration 
file, see the e-terracomm Software Installation and Maintenance Guide). 
• HABConnect request type: For HABCLINK input data sets only, specifies whether data is 
requested individually, as a range, or all the records. 
– Individual: Signals HABCLINK to fetch each data item individually (behavior in 
e-terracomm prior to version 2.3). This request type is suited for a data set 
containing unrelated data in the target database (i.e., referencing a different 
FIELD_RECORD). 
– All: Signals HABCLINK to fetch all instances of the desired FIELD_RECORD in the 
target database, then to match the returned component keys with the data items 
actually listed in the dataset. Every data item in the data set must specify the same 
FIELD_RECORD. Data items do not have to be listed in the same order in the data set 
as in the target e-terrahabitat database, but HABCLINK processes the report from 
SAMPLER more quickly if they are. The transmission style of the data set must be All. 
– Range: Signals HABCLINK to issue a single request for all of the FIELD_RECORD 
instances between the first data item in the dataset and the last data item in the 
dataset. HABCLINK matches the returned component keys with the data items 
actually listed in the dataset. Every data item in the data set must specify the same 
FIELD_RECORD. Data items do not have to be listed in the same order in the data set 
as in the target e-terrahabitat database, but HABCLINK processes the report from 
SAMPLER more quickly if they are. The transmission style of the data set must be All. 
7.3.9.2 Contents 
The CommDataSetDataItem records are used to define the data items or limit sets that 
belong to data sets. These records are used to describe the contents of SCADA (Analogs, 
Status, and Limit Sets), Control Message, Message Object, and Account Request data sets. 
One record per data item or limit set is inserted as a child of the CommDataSet. Only SCADA 
data sets can contain more than one data item or limit set. 
Simply insert a CommDataSetDataItem record and fill the association with the 
CommDataSet parent record. Then fill either the data item or the limit set association. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 454 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
7.3.9.3 Other Considerations 
7.3.9.3.1 Protocol-Specific Modeling 
ICCPLINK Number of CommDataSet DataItem records per data set is limited by the maximum MMS 
PDU size. 
During handshaking, ICCPLINK exchanges with other remote(s) the list of data items in 
the data sets. The list contains the data item names and, for each data item in Domain 
scope, the name of the domain. Depending on the size of the names, the absolute limit 
can be divided almost by a factor of 2. For example, with names of 20 characters and 
domain names of 8 characters, the limit falls to approximately 800, for a PDU size of 
32 K, the maximum supported by ICCPLINK. 
When possible, it is better to have: 
• Short data item names 
• Maximum number of data items in VMD scope (in this case, only the data item name 
is exchanged, not the domain name) 
In any case, GE recommends not having data sets with more than 800 data items. 
The validation program gives an estimate of the PDU size for each data set. When 
exchanging limit sets: 
• It is recommended to have them in separate data sets triggered by exception 
because the limit value does not change very often. 
• When requesting both high and low limits, non–GE remotes requesting limits must 
request them in the order high then low without any other data item in between. 
ISDLINK Does not allow duplicate entries (i.e., the same data item modeled more than once) in 
the same or different data sets. An error is logged when validating the database if 
duplicate entries are found in ISDLINK data sets (only for input data sets because output 
data sets contents are created at run time). 
ELCOLINK The maximum number of CommDataS etDataItem records per data set is 255. 
7.3.10 Priority Pools 
Priority Pool processing is meant to improve the initialization of ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD 
connections when e-terracomm starts up or fails over. Initializing the connections includes 
establishing the TCP/IP connections as well as the protocol handshakes required to get 
data flowing between the EMS and remote systems. 
On very large systems, it can take minutes before the initialization of the ICCP, ELCOM, and 
ISD connections is complete. Often, the connections remain unstable for a long period of 
time, impairing the reception of data from remote systems. Staggering the connections that 
currently exist does not work well, because it relies on the assumptions that all data has the 
same importance and that it takes the same amount of time to complete the handshake for 
each remote; these assumptions are not true. 
Priority Pool processing is optional. When it is used, the remotes need to be grouped in 
“Priority Pools”. Each Priority Pool has a list of remotes. The number of remotes per pool is 
not limited and may contain ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD remotes that are treated in parallel. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 455 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
The number of Priority Pools is not limited. The Priority Pools constitute a list; the first pool in 
the list has the highest priority. When Priority Pool processing is enabled, all the ICCP, 
ELCOM, and ISD remotes must be referenced in the pools. Remotes for other link 
applications must not be modeled in a pool. 
At startup or upon e-terracomm failover, the list of Priority Pools is scanned from the first 
element (highest priority) to the last (lowest priority). For each Priority Pool, the remotes in 
the pool are enabled in sequence. When all pools have been scanned, Priority Pool 
processing is done and is only activated again at the next startup or failover. 
Each pool has a modeled time for determining when it is the next pool’s turn. For the first 
pool, the time countdown starts when ICCP, ELCOM, and ISD applications are ready (on a 
dual system, this is when they receive the enabled role). Only the existing applications are 
checked. Not all systems use the three link applications. 
It is possible to model what happens when a pool’s time elapses: 
• Non-connected remotes, or remotes going up and down, are disabled and re-enabled 
when all pools are finished. 
• Remotes of previous pools are left enabled independently of not being connected or 
going up and down. This is the default option. 
Priority Pool processing works best for master remotes (ICCP or ELCOM); ISD remotes that 
are both master and slave work well. Connection requests received for slave remotes that 
have not yet been enabled by Priority Pool processing are rejected until the pool the 
remotes belong to is active. 
The CommPriorityPool properties are detailed below. 
• Name: User-friendly identification, otherwise not used. 
• Max Time: This is the time the pool is active (i.e., waiting for the remotes in that pool to 
make their connection/handshake). If this is not the last pool, the remotes in the next 
pool(s) are not enabled until the pool they belong to is activated. When the configured 
time elapses, the next pool is activated. If not all remotes of the current pool have 
finished their connection/handshake, they are either disabled until all pools are finished, 
or they continue trying to make their connection/handshake, depending on the global 
parameter “Failed Remotes Are Temporarily NISed”. 
The CommPriorityPoolRemote properties are detailed below. One record is modeled for 
each remote in the pool. 
• Remote: This is the associated remote that belongs to the pool. 
• Number of output data sets: This is the number of output data sets for that remote. 
This field is optional; it is meant to help fine-tune the timing of the pools. 
At run time, the number of active input and output data sets are displayed as they are 
being activated. The display shows the <number of active data sets> / <number of 
modeled data sets>. It is easy to see whether the maximum time for the pool is too long 
(all the expected data sets are active before the maximum time for the pool elapses) or 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 456 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
too short (many data sets are not active when the maximum time elapses). Based on 
that information, the maximum time can be adjusted. 
7.3.11 Cfg Site (SITE) 
This record is used to define the different sites known by Configuration Manager. Note that 
site here is in the context of Configuration Manager, not ISD. 
Initial CfgSite state for first/second site: This field configures how e-terracomm will 
consider the site’s state before any notification from CfgSite.  
7.3.12 ISD Site (RSSITE) 
This record is used to define the name of the ISD sites for each Configuration Manager’s 
site. 
7.4 Quality Mapping 
This section shows mapping of the quality flags between ICCP and other protocols. 
7.4.1 ISD V1.0 thru V3.0 
ISD protocol carries only a few bits among the quality bits handled by SCADA or ICCP. 
• SCADA / ISD status/source bits: 
– SUSPECT: Set if one or more of OLD, BAD, OVER, or NIS is set. 
– REPLACED: Set if either MANREP, GENREP, or ESTREP is set. 
– CMD: For Status Point only, set if the value is a result of a control command (not 
used in ISD versions 1.0 and 1.1). 
– TFAIL: Set if telemetry failed (used in version 1.1 only). 
• ICCP status/source bits: 
– GOOD: Value is valid. 
– HELD: Previous data value has been held over (local interpretation). 
– SUSPECT: Value is questionable. 
– BAD: Value is not valid. 
– TELEMETERED: Value was received from a telemetered site. 
– CALCULATED: Value was calculated based on other data values. 
– MANUAL: Value was entered manually. 
– ESTIMATED: Value was estimated. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 457 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
– NORMAL: Value is the one configured as normal. 
– ABNORMAL: Value is the one configured as abnormal. 
– TSOK: Timestamp reflects when value was last updated. 
– TSBAD: Timestamp does not reflect when value was last updated.

7.4.2 ISD 4.0 and Later 
ISD 4.0 introduced improvements for transferring data attributes (quality, source). 
ISD version 5.0 added BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE, giving information about tags.  
• Value can have the following flags set (status only): 
– MDIS: If set, multiple changes occurred between the reporting of this value and the 
previous value reported. 
– ABNRM: If set, this value represents an abnormal state. 
– BLKOPEN: If set, a tag preventing open operations exists (V5.0). 
– BLKCLOSE: If set, a tag preventing close operation exists (V5.0). 
BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE can be sent/received via ICCP only when Supplemental 
status data objects are supported. 
• Source can be one of the following: 
– TELEM: If set, this data is received via telemetry. 
– CALC: If set, this data value has been calculated based on other data values. 
– MANL: If set, either this data is normally entered manually, or the value has been 
manually replaced. If the value has been manually replaced, the REPL flag is also set. 
– ESTIM: If set, either this data is normally provided from the State Estimator, or the 
value has been provided as a replacement value from the State Estimator. If the 
value has been provided as a replacement value, the REPL flag is also set. 
• Quality: 
– SUSP: If set, this data quality is SUSPECT. This quality can result if the data is out of 
scan on the host computer or if suspect data is provided from an outside source. 
– REPL: If set, this data quality is REPLACED. This quality is reported if the value is an 
operator-overridden value. 
– CMD: If set, this data quality is COMMANDED. This quality occurs if the state was 
altered as the result of a supervisory control request (Status only). 
– INTG: If set, it indicates that this value and quality were sent in response to an 
integrity scan. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 459 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
– TFAIL: If set, this data quality is Telemetry Failed. 
– BAD: If set, this data quality is Bad. This quality can result if the data is in an illegal 
state or if errors were encountered in producing the engineering value. 
– NIS: If set, this data point has been removed from service. 
– OVER (analogs only): If set, this data point is beyond a reasonable range on the 
source system. 
– LONG (counts only): If set, the value associated with this data point is for a time 
range that may be longer than normal, and thus the value may be larger than an 
average reading (for example, a value is returned for an accumulator that is read 
hourly, but the value is for a time range of three hours because of missed readings 
due to telemetry failure or equipment unavailability). 
– BLKSETP: If set, setpoint operations are not allowed (V5.0). This flag is stored in the 
database but is not used (ICCP does not have a way to pass it). 
7.4.2.1 ISD to ICCP Mapping 
Not all ISD quality flags are used in the mapping to ICCP quality because ICCP has many 
fewer flags, and some ISD flags are not even related to quality. The following flags are not 
mapped: TFAIL, OVER, LONG, BLKSETP, INTG, and CMD. 
The ISD ABNRM flag is directly mapped to the ICCP ABNORMAL flag. 
The ISD MDIS flag is processed when MCD processing is configured. 
The ISD flags BLKOPEN and BLKCLOSE are mapped to ICCP only when the data item is of 
type supplemental (type STATUSEX with or without quality and timestamp).

7.4.3 ELCOM-90 
ELCOM-90 has the following quality/source flags: 
• Origin 
– Measured: A point is “measured” when its value is acquired by one of several 
possible measuring methods (e.g., scanning). 
– Manual: The value of a point is “manually entered” when its current value is provided 
by input from an operator or simulator. 
– Estimated: A point is “estimated” when its value is calculated by a State Estimator 
program. 
– Computed: A point is “computed” when its value is the result of a calculation using 
other data (scanned, computed, and/or estimated) as input variables. 
– Held: A point whose value is measured is “held” when the most recent update was 
unsuccessful and an old value is held in the database. 
• Validity 
– OK/Not OK: A point whose value is measured is “OK” when its value was acquired by 
the previous update — i.e., the point is not off-scan, and communications with the 
substation are successful. 
A manually entered value is always “OK”. 
A point whose value is estimated by a State Estimator is “OK” when the State 
Estimator is running at its normal assigned frequency. 
A point whose value is computed is “OK” when all the independent data points from 
which it is computed are “OK”. 
A point whose value is held is always “Not OK”. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 463 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.5 MCD Processing 
The ISD protocol allows passing Multiple Changes Detection information (MDIS flag in status 
message), but the ICCP protocol does not allow a direct mapping of this flag. Instead, ICCP 
can carry the MCD information in two ways: 
• Use of Data_StateExtended (with a “change of value counter” – COV) 
• Use of Data_Discrete (a 32-bit integer) 
The semantics of both are not strictly defined in the ICCP specification. Does the counter 
reflect the number of changes since the last update or since data exchange began? What 
are the possible values for a Data_Discrete when multiple changes are detected? 
The MCD processing in e-terracomm is done in ISDLINK and is configurable on a 
per-remote basis: 
• No MCD processing 
• Delta count 
• Running count 
• Data discrete 
7.5.1 Modeling 
To enable processing of MCD information for a given data item, it must be configured as 
follows: 
• Delta or Running Count 
– The CommDataItem should have the Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value 
Counter flags set to Yes. 
– The CommDataItemPermission for the ISDLINK remote should have the network 
type set to 26 (Status with Quality). 
– The CommDataItemPermission for the ICCPLINK remote should have the network 
type set to 30 (Status with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value Counter). 
• Data Discrete 
– The CommDataItem should have only the Quality flag set to Yes. 
– The CommDataItemPermission for the ISDLINK remote should have the network 
type set to 26 (Status with Quality). 
– The CommDataItemPermission for the ICCPLINK remote should have the network 
type set to 8 (INT32 with Quality). 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 465 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
7.5.2 Processing 
7.5.2.1 Sending MCD Information 
ISDLINK receives the MCD information from the EMS local host, processes it, and passes it 
along with the data item value and quality to OAGSERVE to be stored in the e-terracomm 
database. The data item is then ready to be sent by ICCPLINK to a remote site. 
The processing done by ISDLINK is as follows: 
• Delta or Running Count 
– ISDLINK determines the COV value based on two kinds of information: 
∗ Whether the value changed since last received 
∗ Whether the MCD flag in the received message is set or reset 
The actual number of changes is not known. What is important is that the remote 
sites must be able to determine whether the MCD flag was set or not with the COV 
and point values. The parity of the COV value and whether it is greater than 1 are 
what matters. 
The tables below show how the COV value is set.

7.5.2.1.1 Data Discrete 
If the MCD flag is set in the message received from SCADA, ICCPLINK adds a constant to the 
status value. If the MCD flag is not set, the value is not changed. 
The constant value is 4, which gives a total of 8 possible values for the status. For example: 
0 Between, no MCD 4 Between MCD sets (*) 
1 Open, no MCD 5 Open, MCD set 
2 Closed, no MCD 6 Closed, MCD set 
3 Invalid, no MCD 7 Invalid, MCD set (*) 
(*) These values are unlikely. 
Note that Data Semantics translates only the two lower bits of the value so the MCD 
information is maintained. 
7.5.2.2 Receiving MCD Information 
ICCPLINK receives the MCD information from the remote site. It passes that information 
along with the data item value and quality to OAGSERVE to be stored in the e-terracomm 
database. The data item is then ready to be sent by ISDLINK to the local EMS host. 
Before sending data to EMS, ISDLINK processes MCD information, if any, as follows. 
7.5.2.2.1 Delta or Running Count 
ISDLINK determines whether the MCD flag was set based on two kinds of information: 
• Whether the value changed since last received 
• The COV value 
The MCD flag in the message to SCADA is set or not depending on the two kinds of 
information shown in the following table.

Note that Data Semantics translates only the two lower bits of the value so the MCD 
information is maintained. 
7.6 Filtering Bad Data 
WARNING: Do not use this option if you exchange data with your EMS using ISD protocol 
version 4.0 or later. 
Because the ISD protocol versions 1.0 thru 3.0 have only one quality bit (Good/Suspect), the 
mapping from the richer ICCP quality bits may not reflect the actual “quality” sent to the 
EMS. Also, there is no ICCP “Garbage” quality bit. Due to these deficiencies, it is difficult for 
e-terracomm to indicate to the EMS any degree of confidence on the value of any given 
data. To make matters worse, e-terraplatform uses the value of data even when the quality 
is suspect. 
When a remote value is received via ICCPLINK, the worst quality is BAD, but that does not 
mean that this is not actually garbage. The BAD quality is mapped to ISD Suspect, and the 
EMS may be using garbage values (you notice that by seeing your power applications 
producing bad results or even crashing). 
A workaround is to instruct ISDLINK to not send data with BAD quality to the EMS. To do 
this, set the “Send BAD data to EMS” option to No on the ISDLINK CommRemote record(s). It 
is safe to set this flag when receiving data from an e-terracomm remote because the BAD 
flag is only set when the DB quality is Garbage (i.e., the value must not be used). However, 
other ICCP vendors may send BAD quality with a value that is not really garbage (it may be 
the last known value and the power applications can use it without a problem). 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 468 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
If you want to use BAD data coming from a non–GE remote site, and not use BAD data 
coming from GE remote sites, you can configure different ISDLINK remotes (i.e., SCADA 
sites), mapping them with the ICCPLINK remotes. 
7.7 InterSite Data 4.0 
This section lists the modifications made in the InterSite Data protocol with the introduction 
of version 4.0, and how the modifications are supported in e-terracomm. 
• Added new messages for adding and removing data points from the set of 
measurements passed between sites, without breaking and re-establishing the link or 
otherwise forcing a complete download. 
• Added an integrity scan message to force the source site to send an integrity scan of a 
single measurement, or to send an integrity scan for all measurements mapped 
between the source and destination sites. 
• Modified the function codes of the data messages to identify that the format of the data 
submessages has changed. The new format indicates the type of data passed in each 
submessage, and passes additional quality information. 
• Added a new flag to indicate whether the new state of a status point is abnormal. 
• Added new flags to indicate whether the analog, status, or accumulator data is 
telemetry failed, is a bad reading, or is marked Not In Service. 
• Added data source flags, which are now also passed in the data messages, to indicate 
whether the current data is telemetered, calculated, manually entered, or estimated. 
• Added new extended-data messages that can be returned from the source site. These 
include a time stamp identifying when the value was last modified. The source site 
implementation is responsible for determining the conditions under which the 
extended-data message is returned, instead of the normal data message. 
7.7.1 Adding and Removing Data Points 
e-terracomm supports the request from the EMS to add or remove points in the list of point 
it sends (output data set) with the restriction that, when adding points, these points must 
already exist in the e-terracomm database (i.e., the e-terracomm database should be a 
step ahead of the EMS database). 
7.7.1.1 Adding Data Points 
After checking that the new requested data points exist and have the correct permission 
(Read), e-terracomm adds these points (or a subset if some do not exist) to the output data 
set. They are always added at the end. After adding the data points, an integrity scan is sent 
so the EMS receives the current value of the new points. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 469 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
7.7.1.2 Removing Data Points 
The requested data points are not actually removed from the output data set. Instead, they 
are marked as “deleted” and ISDLINK stops sending them to the EMS. Each deleted entry in 
the output data set as well as the data set itself is displayed in a different color (for details, 
see the e-terracomm User’s Guide – Real-Time Operation). 
The data points are actually removed from the output data set at the next full download. 
7.7.2 Integrity Scan Message 
e-terracomm responds to the EMS request (either for an individual data point or the full set), 
but does not request integrity scans of the EMS. Note that the integrity scan mechanism 
existing in the previous versions of the protocol continues — i.e., an integrity scan is 
automatically performed after a full download or after failed communications are 
re-established. 
7.7.3 New Flags 
The mapping between the new flags and the e-terracomm quality flags is described in 
section 7.4 Quality Mapping. 
7.7.4 Extended Data Messages 
7.7.4.1 Input 
When an extended data message is received from the EMS, the timestamp is sent to 
OAGSERVE to be stored in the database. It is discarded if the data item is not modeled with 
the timestamp attribute set (DB type). 
If the data item is modeled with the attribute timestamp set (DB type) but EMS does not 
send an extended message, ISDLINK timestamps the data at the time it is received from the 
EMS (the millisecond part is always set to 0 in this case). 
7.7.4.2 Output 
If a data item is modeled with the timestamp attribute set (DB type), ISDLINK sends an 
extended message; otherwise, it sends a normal message. 
7.8 InterSite Control 1.0 
This section lists the modifications made in the InterSite Control protocol with the 
introduction of version 1.0, and how the modifications are supported in e-terracomm. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 470 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• Passed version information in each of the four different types of supervisory control 
messages. 
• Added four new messages for sending a control response to each type of supervisory 
control request. Added a placeholder to each of the supervisory control messages. The 
response message is formatted the same as the originating message, except that the 
placeholder field is filled in with an error code identifying the success or failure of the 
control, and an indication of the problem if the control was not successful. 
7.8.1 Version Information 
When the default ISD protocol version modeled on an ISD remote is set to 4.0, ISDLINK 
automatically tries to use InterSite Control 1.0, sending a “Hello” message to Control on the 
EMS. If the EMS does not respond within 5 seconds, ISDLINK assumes that InterSite 
Control 1.0 is not supported by the EMS and it falls back to version 0.0. 
“Hello” messages that are received from the EMS indicating version 1.0 are always 
responded to with a success status. 
7.8.2 Control Response 
In e-terracomm, controls are sent to/received from a remote site using two link 
applications: ISDLINK between the EMS and e-terracomm, and ICCPLINK between 
e-terracomm and a remote site. 
In the ICCP protocol, there is no synchronous control response except when the controlled 
device does not exist, or when other errors such as communication problems are detected 
preventing the remote EMS from initiating the control. Once the control has reached the 
remote EMS, the result of the control is through asynchronous events (ICCP Block 7), 
indicating success or failure. 
ICCPLINK supports Block 7 and is able to forward to ISDLINK control responses that can 
then be sent to the EMS. However, not all ICCP vendors support Block 7 (older versions of 
e-terracomm do not support Block 7 either). Therefore, in this case, it is not possible to send 
the control responses to the EMS. 
When an EMS device is controlled from a remote site, ISDLINK forwards the control 
responses to ICCPLINK, which in turn triggers the success or failure events if the remote site 
supports Block 7 and has requested to receive such events. 
7.9 ICCP 2000-08 vs ICCP 1996-08 
There are not a lot of changes introduced in ICCP 2000–08. Of those changes, only a subset 
are implemented in e-terracomm 2.3.1. 
• New Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data types 
• New way of reporting data changes 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 471 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• Modified/new Block 8 objects 
Note: The ICCP specification has no provision for interoperability between different 
versions — i.e., once a new version is published,  the previous one no longer exists. This is 
not how the “real world” works. It is not possible for a utility with 30 ICCP partners to 
switch simultaneously to a new version of ICCP with its 30 partners. e-terracomm 2.3.1 
supports both versions of ICCP. The version to use must be modeled on a per-remote 
basis. 
7.9.1 New SCADA Data Types 
e-terracomm 2.3.1 supports the new SCADA data types introduced in ICCP 2000–08 as well 
as the Supplemental Objects data types defined in IEC 60870-6-802 Annex B. 
The three new SCADA data types are: 
• INT32 with Quality and Extended Timestamp 
• REAL32 with Quality and Extended Timestamp 
• STATE with Quality and Extended Timestamp 
While the Timestamp has a resolution of one second, the Extended Timestamp has a 
resolution of one millisecond. The Extended Timestamp is made of a 32-bit integer 
representing a time in seconds (GMT time) and a 16-bit integer representing the 
milliseconds. 
The Supplemental Objects data types allow passing more information for status points. The 
following information can be passed: 
• Tag value (0 = No Tag, 1 = Open and Close inhibit, 2 = Close only inhibit) 
• Expected State (2 bits as for the current state) 
The Supplemental Objects data types are: 
• State Supplemental (no attributes) 
• State Supplemental with Quality 
• State Supplemental with Quality and Timestamp 
• State Supplemental with Quality and Extended Timestamp 
• State Supplemental with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value Counter 
In e-terracomm 2.3.1, the Supplemental Objects data types can be modeled. However, the 
Tag value and Expected State are just displayed; there is no processing of these fields. A 
future version of the ISD protocol will provide a way of sending them to and receiving them 
from the EMS. 
The new data types are modeled and displayed as indicated in the following table.

7.9.2 New Way of Reporting Data Changes 
With ICCP version 1996–08, only the last value is reported with any kind of data set trigger 
(PER/EXC/REQ) or style (ALL/RBE). 
ICCP version 2000–08 introduces the ability to report all changes that have occurred during 
a modeled buffering time — i.e., multiple instances of a given data item can be reported in a 
single report. 
ISDLINK has always been able to do this for status (the buffering time is actually the polling 
interval of the EMS). However, to work properly, it was necessary to modify OAGSERVE to 
not do the buffering time monitoring because changed values were replacing previous ones 
in the database during the buffering time. The buffering time needs to be done by the link 
application to allow maintaining a buffer with all the changes. 
The change in OAGSERVE had already been done when ELCOLINK was implemented 
(ELCOM-90 allows reporting all changes), and a new trigger type (UDT) was introduced to 
instruct OAGSERVE to pass received changes from the source of the data (input data set) 
immediately to the destination(s) of the data (output data set(s)). 
The same new trigger is now allowed for ICCPLINK and ISDLINK data sets (for ISDLINK, only 
for output data sets). It is not necessary for input data sets because ISDLINK already reports 
changes for a given data item separately. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 473 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
Note: The name of the trigger, “UDT”, comes from ELCOM-90 and stands for “Unsolicited 
Data Transfer”. 
To model such data reports from a remote ICCP up to the EMS, the ICCPLINK input data set 
must have Trigger=UDT, Style=RBE, and a non-zero exception buffering time (a zero 
exception buffering time generates a report for every single change). The ISDLINK output 
data set has the same trigger and style (UDT, RBE). The exception buffering time does not 
matter (the time changes are buffered before they are sent to the EMS depending on the 
EMS polling interval). 
To model such data reports from the EMS to an ICCP remote, the ISDLINK input data set is 
(as usual) Trigger=PER, Style=RBE. 
The ICCPLINK output data set is created and enabled by the remote site. The remote needs 
to enable the data set with the “AllChangesReported” flag set to True in the TransferSet. 
For e-terracomm remotes, the input data set must be modeled with Trigger=UDT and 
Style=RBE. Setting the trigger to UDT instructs ICCPLINK to set the “AllChangesReported” 
flag to True in the TransferSet used to remotely enable the data set. 
7.9.3 Modified and New Block 8 Objects 
The Transfer Account object has been modified to include the field TransactionCode, and 
two new objects have been added: General Data Report and General Data Response. 
As of e-terracomm 2.3.1, the implementation of these changes has been deemed 
unnecessary due to the lack of procurement for Block 8 support. 
ICCP Block 8 is not supported with ICCP version 2000–08 (error in validation if configured), 
but it continues to be supported with ICCP version 1996–08. 
7.10 Special Modeling 
This section describes the specific modeling of Account and Information Messages objects 
(ICCP Blocks 8 and 4), and Control messages. 
• Account objects are supported by ICCPLINK and ISDLINK. 
• Information messages are supported by ICCPLINK and ISDLINK. 
• Control messages are supported by ICCPLINK, ELCOLINK, and ISDLINK. 
7.10.1 Modeling Information Messages 
Figure 116 describes the modeling of information messages exchanged, in both directions, 
between two remotes: KENT and AUBURN. Only the configuration at KENT is detailed. In the 
figure below, AUBURN is shown as GE’s e-terracomm. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 474 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
 
Figure 116. Information Messages 
The KENT site configuration has a scheduling application, a messaging application, and 
e-terracomm. The messaging application exchanges messages, using ICCP, with a remote 
site located at AUBURN. KENT receives one message (Information Reference = 6755) from 
AUBURN, and also sends a message (Information Reference = 6754) to AUBURN. 
1. CommDataItem: For each message, define a CommDataItem record with type 
Information Message, and with Size set to the maximum number of bytes that might 
ever be used by the Information Message plus 14 (ICCP Information Message header). 
The other required data item fields must also be filled in. The data item name (either the 
identification or the optional name depending on the data item configuration) must be a 
number; this number is the Information Reference that identifies the Information 
Message. 
2. Input CommDataSet: For each Information Message, create an Input data set as a child 
of the Source remote. The trigger must be On Request, and the transmission style must 
be All. 
3. Input CommDataSetDataItem: Insert a CommDataSetDataItem record for each input 
data set and associate it with the data item created in step 1. 
4. Output CommDataSet: For each Information Message, insert an Output data set as a 
child of the destination remote. The trigger must be On Receipt, and the transmission 
style must be All. 

 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 475 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
5. Output CommDataSetDataItem: Insert a CommDataSetDataItem record for each 
output data set and associate it with the same data item created in step 1. 
6. On the CommDataSets records, fill in the Twin field for both Input and Output data sets 
so they reference each other. 
7. Fill in the rest of the Input and Output data sets as necessary. 
7.10.2 Modeling Control Messages 
Figure 117 describes the modeling of controls exchanged, in both directions, between two 
remotes: KENT and AUBURN, and in one direction between RENTON and KENT. Only the 
configuration at KENT is detailed. 
 
Figure 117. Control Configuration 
Among other data, KENT’s EMS sends SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 to AUBURN 
and RENTON, and receives SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 from AUBURN. 
Devices are associated with the data so they can be remotely controlled. KENT controls 
SCADA2_ANALOG1 (Setpoint) and SCADA2_STATUS2 (Open/Close) while AUBURN and 
RENTON can control SCADA1_ANALOG1 (Setpoint) and SCADA1_STATUS1 (Open/Close). 

 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 476 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
Devices associated with SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 are Select Before 
Operate (SBO). 
Devices associated with SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 are Direct Operate (DO). 
1. CommDataItems: Control commands require two-way communication between the 
controlling remote and the remote source of the device (i.e., the source of the data item 
with which the device is associated). The data items are used to carry control requests 
and responses. Each data item can carry a request or a response, meaning that if each 
remote sends control to the other one, the same data items can be used both ways. 
For the KENT site to be able to control SCADA2_ANALOG1 and SCADA2_STATUS2 at 
AUBURN, you need two data items: one with source KENT and the other with source 
AUBURN. These two data items also allow the AUBURN site to control 
SCADA1_ANALOG1 and SCADA1_STATUS1 at KENT. You do not need other data items. 
For the RENTON site to also be able to control SCADA1_ANALOG1 and 
SCADA1_STATUS1, you need two more data items: one with source RENTON and the 
other with source KENT. Set Write permission for the source remote and Read 
permission for the non-source remote. 
2. Input CommDataSets: Under each remote that sends or receives control, insert an 
Input data set for the other remote with which it exchanges control messages. In our 
configuration: 
– Remote SCADA: Two Input data sets, one for AUBURN and one for RENTON. 
– Remote AUBURN: One Input data set for SCADA. 
– Remote RENTON: One Input data set for SCADA. 
The trigger must be On Request, and the transmission style must be All. 
3. Input CommDataSetDataItems: For each Input data set, insert a 
CommDataSetDataItem record; associate it with the data item created in step 1. The 
data item is the one with source = parent remote of the Input data set (e.g., for the 
SCADA_CTRL_IN data set, the ENTRY must reference the CTRL1 data item because its 
source is the SCADA remote, parent of the data set). This is also the data item with Write 
permission for the data set’s parent remote. 
4. Output CommDataSets: Repeat step 2, this time inserting an Output data set. The 
trigger type must be On Receipt, and the transmission style must be All. 
5. Output CommDataSetDataItems: For each Output data set, insert a 
CommDataSetDataItem record. Associate it with the data item created in step 1. The 
data item is the one with Read permission for the Output data set’s parent remote. 
6. On the CommDataSet records, fill in the Twin field for both Input and Output data sets 
so they reference each other. 
7. Fill in the rest of the Input and Output data sets as necessary. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 477 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

7.10.3 Component Status Data Items 
There are two types of component data items: 
• Topology component data items 
• Data set component data items 
7.10.3.1 Topology Component Data Items 
These data items are created automatically by the database validation program. 
In this context, a “component” is a topology component: CommLinkApplication, 
CommRemote, CommLink, or CommPath. For each component, the validation program 
creates a CommDataItem. At run time, OAGSERVE deposits a coded number representing 
the current status of the component. The identification of a Component Status data item is 
formed by appending the component’s ID to a conventional prefix. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 478 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
Component Prefix 
LNKAPP ASTS_ 
REMOTE RSTS_ 
LINK LSTS_ 
PATH PSTS_ 
The remote source of such data items is set to OAGSERVE (“pseudo remote”). 
If an ISDLINK remote exists in the database, the validation program creates an ISD optional 
name: 
<SUBSTN> <DEVTYP> <DEVICE> <POINT> 
where: 
• SUBSTN = ID of the link application (under which the component is) 
• DEVTYP = “OAG” 
• DEVICE = ID of the component 
The ID is truncated to the first 14 characters, so be aware that it is possible that the 
truncation will create duplicate device names (the database validation issues a warning 
when truncation happens). 
• POINT = Prefix depending on the component type (as shown above, but without the 
underscore) 
No data sets are automatically defined to contain Component Status data items. The user 
can reference them like any other SCADA data item when defining a data set. 
If you want to exchange Component Status data items using ISDLINK, the network type for 
ISDLINK remotes must be set to “STATUS-Q-T”. This is actually done by the validation 
program. 
The Component Status data items can have the following values: 
State Value 
Up 2 = ICCP_STATUS_CLOSED 
Down 1 = ICCP_STATUS_TRIPPED 
Out of Service 8 = When sent to the EMS vi a ISD, 0 is passed, which is equivalent 
to ICCP_STATUS_BETWEEN. 
Returned to Service 
(*) 
1 = Down = ICCP-STATUS_TRIPPED 
(*) This state is specified only to clearly indicate that when the component is put back into service, there are 
two state transitions: “Out of Service” to “Down” and “Down” to “Up”. 
If you change the ID of one or more components between runs of the validation program, 
new data items are created with the new ID, and the data items with the previous ID are 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 479 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
automatically deleted (a warning is logged for every Status data item that has been 
deleted). If Status data items are exchanged in data sets, and you change the ID of a 
component, remember to also change the ID in the data set (Data Set Contents display). 
You can change the automatically generated ISD optional name of a component data item. 
7.10.3.2 Data Set Component Data Items 
The data set component data items are not automatically created. They need to be 
modeled. 
For each Input data set you want to report the state to the EMS, you need to model a data 
item as any other SCADA data item, and reference this data item in the data set (field Data 
Item for Data Set state). The specific settings for the data item are as follows: 
• Name: No restrictions 
• Database type: Integer 32-bit with Quality, Timestamp, and Change of Value counter 
• ISDLINK optional name: As needed for the EMS modeling 
• Source: Must be OAGSERVE 
• Permissions: Read for the ISDLINK remote on which the data item is sent to the EMS 
• Network type: Status with Quality and Timestamp for the ISDLINK remote on which the 
data item is sent to the EMS 
The Data Set Component data items can have the following values: 
State Value 
Active (enabled and received as expected) 2 = ICCP_STATUS_CLOSED 
Not Active (out of service, not yet remotely 
enabled) 
1 = ICCP_STATUS_TRIPPED 
Late (enabled but not being received as expected) 0 = ICCP-STATUS_BETWEEN 
7.11 e-terracomm Model Validation Rules 
Many of the e-terracomm model validation rules are implemented in the attribute and 
association definitions of the metadata entity (such as data range, string length, and 
association cardinality). Those model rules are enforced during data entry. In addition to 
those data entry rules, the following rules are defined in the validation modules that are 
only triggered as part of full validation and e-terracomm model validation. 
7.11.1 Comm Auxiliary Validation Module 
The following validation is performed using SQL directly in the database. The rules being 
validated are not as visible as those that are defined in the Validation Rules modeling. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 480 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• PriorityPoolWithSameRemote: Error if the same remote has been found multiple times in 
the Priority Pool modeling (either in the same pool or a different pool, or both). 
• NonReferencedRemote: Error if not all ISD, ELCOM, and ICCP remotes are referenced in 
priority pools. 
• CommSiteWithNoIsd: Error if a CommCfgSite does not have at least one CommIsdSite 
pair. 
• CommRemoteNoProtocol: Error if a remote does not specify which protocol is used. 
• CommRemoteWithNoPath: Error if a CommRemote does not have at least one 
CommPath. 
• CommLinkAppWithSameType: Error if more than one LNKAPP record is found with the 
same linkappType. 
• CommDupName: Error if duplicated names are found within LNKAPP and/or global 
items. 
• CommDupLimSetNameOnISD: Error if duplicate ICCPName is found when any 
ISD_LNKAPP is True and SDINAME_ITEMS is False. 
• CommDataSetDiffEntries: Error if DSDEF and its twin do not match for all of its children 
entries. 
• CommDataSetNoTwin: Error if the DSDEF has no twin. 
• CommRemoteDupDataSet: Error if the REMOTE has two DSDEFs with the same ID. 
7.11.2 Comm Model Validation Module 
This validation is performed using standard Validation Rules modeling within the metadata. 
The metadata can be examined for additional details about each of these rules. 
• CommDataConvDataItemNoDI: Error if the CommDataConversion column in the

• CommDataItemNoType: Error if the NameType column in the CommDataItemName 
record is null.

not match.

Proprietary – See Copyright Page 481 e-terracomm Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
• CommDataSetInvalidExcTimer: Error if the DataSetTrigger value is equal to EXC, the

• CommDataSetNoTrigger: Error if the DataSetTrigger is null in the CommDataSet record. 
• CommInvalidIntegrityTime: Error if the DataSetTrigger value is equal to PER, the 
IntegrityTimer value is not null or zero, and the IntegrityTime value is less than or equal 
to PerTimer in the CommDataSet record. 
• CommInvalidPerTimer: Error if the DataSetTrigger value is equal to PER and the

• CommLinkAppNoType: Error if LinkApplicationType is null in the CommLinkApplication

• CommLinkWithNoPath: Error if there are no children CommPath records in the

• CommNoDataItem: Error if there are no CommDataItem records. 
• CommNoDataSet: Error if there are no CommDataSet records. 
• CommNoLink: Error if there are no CommLink records. 
• CommNoLinkApp: Error if there are no CommLinkApplication records. 
• CommNoPath: Error if there are no CommPath records. 
• CommNoRemote: Error if there are no CommRemote records.

• CommPriorityPoolRemoteTypeInvalid: Error if RemoteType is not equal to ISDLINK,

• CommQualityMapICCPAny: Error if the Direction column value is equal to ICCPTOISD, the 
ICCPQuality column value is equal to ANY, and the ICCPSource column value is equal to

• CommQualityMapISDAny: Error if the Direction column value is not equal to ICCPTOISD, 
the ISDQuality column value is equal to ANY, and the ISDSource column value is equal to 
ANY in the CommQualityMap record. 
• CommRemoteIdInvalid: Error if the Name column value is equal to OAGSERVE in the 
CommRemote record. 
• CommRemoteWithNoLink: Error if the CommRemote record has no children CommLink 
records.

e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide

8.3.1 TAGGING Configuration 
This contains the global parameters for the TAGGING application. Follow the description for

• USE IMS: e-terraplatform 3.0 uses the Identifier Mapping Service to provide the

On production systems it is highly recommended to set this to Yes. Note that tags and 
tagged objects created on a system not using IMS are not compatible with a system 
that is using IMS, due to MRID incompatibility. 
• USE DATA Service: This option is currently disabled, as data service is not available in 
e-terraplatform 3.0. 
• IMS Resynchronization Interval: When the MRID of a tagged object cannot be verified 
because IMS is not available, this setting provides the interval in seconds between each 
attempt to verify the MRID. 
• Number of Comment Lines: When a comment is changed (when creating, deleting, or 
modifying a tag), TAGGING logs the comment’s content. The log might become 
overloaded when operators enter long comments. TAGGING uses this setting to 
truncate the comments in the log (displayed with ellipses). Full content is still accessible 
in the tagging displays. 
• Longname Prefix: When no long name is available, TAGGING creates its own long name 
based on the object’s composite key. This setting is used as the prefix for this created 
long name (e.g., Longname, LN ...). 
8.3.2 TAGGING Expiration 
Expiration time is used to automatically remove a tag after a specified duration. Default 
expiration can be defined on the tag types, but this list is mainly used in the tag popup. 
8.3.3 TAGGING Communication 
This models an ISTSITE site. IST is the intersite Tagging protocol used to exchange tag 
information between two tagging applications. 
TAGGING supports only two sites: the local site and the remote one. 
• Is the Site Independent?: If Yes, this setting indicates that the peer site that TAGGING is 
connected with can be simultaneously active. If No, then only one site is active at a time. 
For example, this can be used between an EMS and a DTS, or between TAGGING running 
on a production system and another one used as display backup. 
 
Proprietary – See Copyright Page 488 TAGGING Modeling 
e-terrasource EMS Modeling Guide 
8.3.4 TAGGING GrpTypes 
This models the type of group supported by the TAGGING application. 
8.3.5 TAGGING TagTypes 
This models the tag types of the application. 
Use the TAGGING/behavior grouping to set the restriction(s) on the record. These 
restrictions are not managed by TAGGING, but are sent to the TAGGING clients. The client 
will interpret these attributes according to its processing. For example, Block close is used 
only by applications that manage statuses and can detect if the status is opened or closed, 
and that can issue controls. e-terrascada is one example. 
8.3.6 TAGGING Datasources 
The datasource tells TAGGING what source will be using TAGGING data and what this 
source can handle. 
8.3.6.1 Datasource 
• Host1: This is used for datasources that TAGGING needs to know how to contact, such 
as e-terradistribution. For datasources that use NETIO on the same NNI as the TAGGING 
application, you do not need to provide this setting. Specify localhost in this case. 
8.3.6.2 Tagable Record Type 
Unlike SCADAMOM, where tagable record types were hardcoded as masks, TAGGING is free 
to receive any record types for the given data source.  
Note the following: 
• TAGGING will not verify in the datasource schema that these record types exist. 
• The default tagtype should be an applicable tagtype. 
8.3.6.3 Applicable Tagtypes 
This gives the list of all tagtypes that can be applied to the record type.
